title: Batman - The Telltale Series
text: Another solid title from Telltale, this time focusing on Batman. This isn't exactly an origin story, in that Batman has obviously been operating for at least a while, but it's still early days. Harvey Dent is still DA, his relationship with Gordon is still a bit rocky...things like that. This is definitely a non canon story though and I really don't mind that, some of the better Batman stories I've read have been alternate takes on the Dark Knight, and while some things are going to annoy people (Perhaps one twist especially) I found them intruiging and fascinating. If you have ever played a Telltale game before, you know what to expect gameplay wise, conversation choices mixed in with quick time event action. Cinematically and narratively, this is good work from Telltale. The narrative is consistently engaging and the action scenes are tense and well choreographed. An interesting twist is that on a few occasions, you will have the choice to go to a certain scene either as Bruce Wayne or as Batman, basically a choice between diplomacy or intimidation and violence. I actually quite enjoyed the focus a little more on Bruce as mostly he is kind of in the background, his relationship with Harvey was quite well developed and you get a feeling for their friendship. Other characters are well realised too, Alfred and Gordon are excellent as always and there is a really frefreshing take on the Penguin. Also worth mentioning is the new villian, who I also found quite compelling. Anyway, to say more about the plot would spoil the fun. The cartoon graphics are excellent and really capture the grimyness of Gotham. That said, this is the Telltale engine, so their are occasion framerate hickups and a few animationg glitches. It's nothing deal breaking, but god I hope these guys make a full blown new engine soon. Sound and music are excellent, as is the voice acting. In conclusion, I really enjoyed Telltale's Batman. It is not their greatest game (In my bias opinion that's Tales from the Borderlands) but its still a solid ride and I really can't wait to see where they go with season 2) 8 out of 10

title: Batman - The Telltale Series
text: Really wanted to love this and be able to recommend it but I'm afraid I can't.  However if season 2 is a belter you'll probably need to play this first.  And in fairness it's not that bad, it just has some major flaws and appears really buggy, even a whole year on.  Which is a shame as Telltale is a studio I have a lot of time for. I know a lot of people will complain that choices don't matter, and the major story milestones are set in stone.  That's fine for me.  What I can't forgive is where there are instances of obvious ignoring of my choices and the application of the opposite of what I choose just to keep the story on rails e.g. I specifically did not tell vicki vale a suspect's name, and then later on in the game t says I did.  Or when Gordon calls Batman a hero in one scene and then threatens to lock him up the next with no obvious cause inbetween.  Why give me the choice in the first place if it's going to be stamped on later?  Or they'll show a scene that will be in an upcoming episode which never comes to be.  Now I could accept that if I had played the game as they were releasing each episode one at a time but I'm playing this long after all episiodes were out!  Also the dialogue can be a bit odd at times, with tone and attitude of characters shifting all over the place, and conversations seeming quite unnatural.  They should have taken the time to ensure the quality was there, and instead it all looks rather rushed and amateurish. The game also suffers some major technical problems.  Whole scenes will play out with only audio and a black screen, or frozen on a weird graphical oddity.  Sound effects don't tie in with actions.  Sound effects can be missing.  Lip sync can be all over the place.  Recurring stuttering.  An odd freeze on the last frame of scenes before it cuts away elsewhere.  This all seemed to get worse as I went on with Episode 5 being borderline unplayable. The scene pacing was a bit too fast for me as well.  I'm more used to the more recent batman films, the gotham series, and the recent batman games, and the game flits from scene to scene with barely time to gather your breath, and some plot points really stretch the limits of believable logic at times. What the game has to be commended for though is that the QTEs, a bane in most other types of games, actually work quiet well here.  Also, the story itself, barring some minor points, as a whole is rather pleasing.  They have not been afraid to play around in the lore of the Batman universe, and change some things about, the majority of which I can't say for fear of spoilers.  I liked fact they had gone and done things like given Penguin an English accent and actually made it make sense within the story. So all in all, it's a rather unfortunate affair.  If you love telltale and you love batman you will get some enjoyment from this.    But there are better telltale games and better batman games out there.  If you want to get into telltale, go elsewhere, check out the Wolf Among Us, or The Walking Dead.  And if you want Batman check out any of the Batman Arkham games.

title: Batman - The Telltale Series
text: As an experienced player of Telltale games I jumped into this title not expecting too much. Telltale have made very similar games for a few years now and they keep the concept going mostly steady. After a few letdowns with some previous titles I didn't really set my bar high for this game. However, im glad to say I was very impressed by this game and the improvement Telltale has made to this title. This game features a good set of hard choices to make, however it's hard to say how much inpact it will have for the future, but they are really tricky and you have to stop and think for many of them. The choices (without spoiling) were most of the time pretty equal in procent between players choosing A or B, meaning that more people then me found that there was a lot of hard picks to make. I learned a lot about the villains from another perspective in this game, like catwoman, two-face and joker before they got their role. You get the chance to try and change who they become and which you wanna help or try and become friend with. It's a very interesting perspective, especially since the other batman games only follows a set line where the villains are bad guys, while this game let you make more decisions and learn to know them better. This give you as the player more feelings for them and it's an effective way of doing story-telling. This is a game focused on Bruce Wayne, his family legacy and a lot of things I didn't know came up. I have played all the other batman games and watched the movies, however I haven't read the comics so I still have missed a lot. Therefore it's hard for me to compare the two and whats completely new and what is taken from the comics. But this game added a lot more for me even as someone who have played previous games, as it doesn't focus as much on the joker and more about the events before the other games. A new villain is also included in this game, which is refreshing since Joker made many appearances in the other batman games. I won't spoil who this new villain is, but let me just say its very interesting and the story takes many turns in directions I didn't see coming. Telltale is extremely good at making you like characters to later be screwed over by them or killed. This is something they have done in previous games as well and you can roleplay as more of a good guy, evil and mean, or try and be neutral. I haven't seen Telltale make the decisions, choices and characters feel this impactful since The Walking Dead, which is a very good thing, for those of you who haven't played that title. It's very exciting and more interesting to play the Telltale's Tales From The Borderlands for example, in my opinion. The QTE's have been improved I would say. I feel like there's less fighting in this game then the others and more focus on dialogue, but there's still a decent amount of it, so stay away if you hate QTE (quick time events - basically pushing buttons in a said order). They made it better and somehow makes it feel impactful in the fights, but of course the story is the strong point of this title. Batman is known for solving crimes and searching for clues on crime scenes. Well like the other batman games you have some of that in this game as well. It's pretty simple but fun anyway and it's a welcome change in gameplay from just QTE's. You can play the game with keyboard + mouse or with a controller. I played most of the game with an xbox controller since it's mostly a game you can kick back and watch, like an interactive movie where you press buttons once in a while. But whatever you choose to play with works. The game runs at 60 fps locked and I think they have improved upon the PC-port, options menu and graphics since previous games. The style is the same but some better textures for example. They also give you some more choice this time around, for example you can pick the colour of your gear which will be unique for your playthrough. The episodes are between 1-2 hours each, the first one is always a bit longer. Five episodes in total so you are looking at about 6-10 hours, depends on how fast you figure out the clues and how much you look around. I can't say I have any complaints about this game, I'm actually very impressed! I would put this among my top Telltale games actually and give it a big recommendation to fans of point 'n' click, Telltale games in general or fans of Batman and superheroes. Love it!

title: Batman™: Arkham Origins
text: TL;DR: JUST SHUT UP AND FEED YOUR MONEY INTO THE DISC DRIVE UNTIL THE GAME STARTS DOWNLOADING. No, in all seriousness... The game is good. Much of the actual gameplay is the same as what you find in Arkham City, but the story at least makes it worth playing, especially if you're new to the series. It's also a pretty decent PC port. It runs well, and the keyboard and mouse work well too, but some menus are lacking full mouse support. I'd recommend a controller if you have access to one, but it's probably not worth running out and buying one for it. In conclusion, I'd recommend buying it, whether you're new to the Arkham series or a long-time fan--But if you're new, do yourself a favour and go pick up the other games after you beat this one. Dear god where to begin... In terms of gameplay the game feels literally just like Arkham City. Everything you knew and loved is there(though many of it goes by different names, and there have been several improvements), from the line-launcher to the freeze grenades, hell, even the grapnel boost makes a return--though it's worth mentioning that unlike City, almost all of your gadgets except the batarang and the bat claw must be unlocked through the story. This is both a blessing and a curse. On the one hand, returning players will feel right at home with Origins, but on the other, returning players expecting a new experience will be left wanting. Having entirely completed Arkham City on console in the past, I can tell you that I DEFINITELY didn't enjoy Arkham Origins for its combat, or its puzzles. The addition of skills that do things like double your damage for perfectly time your blows, the addtion of the shock gauntlets, and forcing you to unlock basically all of your takedown moves and gadgets as you go along made combat marginally more interesting, but the change is superficial at best. At the end of the day, you're basically the same old Bat by the half-way mark, and considering how much combat is in the game, that's less than ideal for me. But that doesn't by any means make Origins a bad game. The addition of more casefiles to solve, the intense bossfights with the assassins, and the AMAZING storyline make it totally worth playing. The casefiles are usually a lot shorter and simpler than they were in City, with each one usually lasting 5 to 10 minutes max, not counting the trek from point A to point B to collect the perpetraitor. All the casefiles I've seen so far sans one have been a murder, but the one that wasn't turned into one almost immediately. They're fun as hell though, and there are lots of ways to kill people, so it hasn't run dry for me yet. Outside of those more mundane every-day crimes, you do see the return of several of your favourite arch-enemies from City, such as the Mad Hatter. I don't think anyone will disagree with me when I say that outside of the story, the bossfights are one of the biggest reasons to play this game. They're challenging, fun, and just satisfying as all hell. There's a ridiculous amount of variety in them, more than you'd expect considering what they are, and each boss has to be tackled in an entirely different way. Deadshot becomes a predator challenge, Deathstroke is a 1v1 duel, and Copperhead... Well, I don't want to give too much away, but Copperhead is probably one of my new favourite bosses in any game. Getting back ONTO the story though, that's probably THE number one reason to play this game. It's just fantastic. It's totally unique, and has a twist half-way through that I never saw coming. So far no two missions have been remotely similar, and I can't find a single thing to complain about. One thing I feel like I should mention as I close down this wall of text is the lack of Hamill and Conroy in their usual roles in the Arkham series. As anyone who was following the series will know, Warner Bros Montreal didn't even approach the two stars for the roles of Joker and Batman, because they wanted the characters to sound much younger in the game. And all I have to say is.... Mission bloody well accomplished. I'll be honest, there have legitimately been times where I HAVE FORGOTTEN that I wasn't listening to Conroy and Hamill in this game. Troy Baker and Roger Smith sound ridiculously similar to young Conroy and Hamill--And I mean RIDICULOUSLY similar. Frankly, I'm envious of the impressions. They even nail the smallest mannerisms--well, most of the time. Every now and then things start to sound a little off, but it's usually pretty hard to notice once you really get into the story. In conclusion, it's a good game. I wouldn't say it's great, but it's worth owning, and it's a worthy addition to the Arkham series. In terms of the quality of the port, there isn't much to say. The game runs fine, and for the most part keyboard & mouse works well, but a controller wouldn't be a bad idea. There are a few occasions where the buttons feel awkward, and a few menus where the mouse doesn't work, but it's tollerable. Just make sure you rebind those damn quicklaunch keys. :P

title: Batman™: Arkham Origins
text: Comparing this game to Arkham Asylum (AA) and Arkham City (AC). Prior knowledge of these would be preferable if you want to get the most out of this review. Combat: Pretty much the same as AC. If you liked that improved version over AA then you're pretty much golden. I think the overall number of enemies you fight at once is a bit lower though. The downside here is that the base game offers also exactly the same types of enemies (standard, armored, gun or melee weapon) and the same ways to combat them. It's pretty much 100% the same game in terms of combat, which might have been a bit of a missed opportunity. Gadgets: Same as combat. You have access to pretty much the same gadget as in AC with 1 notable exception: The line launcher is gone and replaced by a different version. You can now only use it on certain anchor points but you can also use it to do takedowns, etc. Apart from that cryo bombs are glue bombs, but work exactly the same. Again, no improvements or differences. Graphics: Also no noticable differences to AC. Setting: Even the setting is basically the same as AC. The map seems to have been expanded a bit and some land marks in my opinion are at another place than in the AC map, but apart from that you're still going to see the Church, the Courthouse, the GCPD, the Steel Mill, etc. Of course this Gotham has not been turned into a prison yet, but even Wonder Tower is there, but not accessible. The most notable differences here are the Gotham Bridge and some in building areas like the Hotel. Of course it's winter again...what's nice though is that there's no more maze like underground complex. Overall it's ok, but not ground breaking. Collectibles: This might be a plus for some, but a negative point for others. Personally I like that the number of collectibles has been SIGNIFICANTLY reduced compared to AC. More than AA, but not too many. You're also not going to have too much of a hard time collecting them all, because as in AC you can interrogate Riddler's men to get the location of the "extortion data" (no trophies this time) and most are quite easy to spot when you know where to look for. Some require some rudimentary puzzle skills, but if you've played AC those won't pose any kind of problem. The informants are also conveniently placed on your map and by the time you have acquired all gadgets you will only have to backtrack to like 3 inside locations (or 4 perhaps) and you know you'll have them all. It's more convenient than AC. There's also some "tags" to scan for Gotham story information. And you can scan some "plaques" for a short side quest. These are however not displayed on your map, so it's up to you to find them all. Gone are the riddles though, which is kind of a shame, since those very quite fun. Overall you will still have to invest a few hours to "catch them all". Crime scenes: These are also back again, but have been improved over AC. There's still not much player input or thinking required, but they're well presented. Side missions: These are this time centered around 8 "individuals", small quest lines so to speak. They're a nice distraction and give you some information into the up and coming bad guys for the most part. One of them can only be started after the game has been beaten. Story (possible spoilers below): The story is overall good I'd say. Some characters don't get to shine enough, some are "different". Boss fights: Initially the story revolves around you being targeted by 6 Hitmen (Electrocutioner, Deathstroke, Shiva, Firefly, Bane, Copperhead plus Killer Croc as an added bonus). The boss fights are for the most part rather boring and badly executed to be honest. More below: Overall the game is ok, but not brilliant. It also still has quite a few bugs. Thankfully those could all be resolved by reloading a check point...but still. Multiplayer: Just the same as AC really, but you get to fight as Deathstroke for whatever reason as well. Why not the other bad guys too? And make them a bit more different...Deathstroke feels different. He's weightier. Apart from that there's just Bruce Wayne as a DLC character...yay DLC: Apart from Cold Cold Heart it's forgettable, unless you want to heavily dive into MP. One DLC adds Bruce Wayne as a playble character into the MP game...yay. He plays a bit like Catwoman from AC, but I had honestly hoped this would be about Bruce Wayne becoming Batman as the title suggests...nope. Cold Cold Heart: This DLC puts you up against Mr. Freeze. It's actually quite enjoyable apart from the increased difficulty. I have no idea why it's not possible to change the difficulty of the DLC in Arkham games, because if you just want to enjoy the game you're out of luck. The DLC is definitely not on "easy", meaning you die with about 4 gunshots and somehow countering is also less forgiving. The overall story is nice, the presentation as well, but it drags on a bit. The final boss fight, however, is a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ It is reminiscent of the fight against Freeze in AC, but not nearly executed as well...missed opportunities.

text: Forget what they say about this game. Most of the bugs are fixed. The only that still exist is: Gliding makes batman go up and down (just dive for a sec and it stops). Baddies sometimes have some trouble with stairs. There is a REALLY SMALL chance that the floor won't load (only on the exterior territories) just load the last saved point it   will be instantly fixed. (you will lose one minute of your life). Also i have seen some (with low play time) complain that the game stops to load each territory if you glide through the map quickly. This will happen only once or twice the first time you ever get to those locations. Just endure it. Now back to the game itself. I gotta say (unlike others) this must be the best Batman game till now. The biggest Pros are: Boss fights feel like Boss fights. In the other arkham games most of them needed one or 2 tries and felt insignificant. Not in Origins, they feel strong , they feel badass and definitely pack a punch. (on Hard at least). Most epic cinematics. The combat is reaaally better. Plus the Shock gloves are epic. There are many new ways to take-down in Stealth which is so immersive. You feel like a true predator. There is a mini-quest list, which awards you for utilising more complex tools or for getting better with either experience (for awesome upgrades) or with some upgrades themselves. The story may seem a bit dull at first but seeing how age affects every villain and Batman (if you compare them to the other Arkham games) and how some came to be the ones we know is just amazing. (Probably cause i'm a sucker for origins :X) Not to mention how i haven't yet finished the main game with 18+ hours (haven't even touched the Dr.Freeze dlc yet). Also the side-quests introduce more villains and or inform you about how Batman got his friendly relationship with Barbara etc. (And there are more than the other Batman games). TL:DR I harshly exceed the minimum requirements but this hasn't stopped me for loving the game which shows a lot.

title: Batman™: Arkham Origins
text: Batman Arkham series is held high for perfect depiction of Batman universe. Arkham City is considered the best Arkham game in the franchise and Arkham Origins is nearly ignored for being lame. But its not correct. This is as good as Arkham City. Arkham Origins takes you through the initial years of Bruce Wayne as Batman. It is a direct prequel to Arkham Asylum. The best thing about Origins is the story/game progression. I will term it 'epic'. You may think the starting pace is little slow, but as it progresses it becomes very intriguing and at times emotional. I adore its storyline! To play this story, you get a bigger playground ....map bigger than Arkham City. And the time.....its Christmas eve! Who doesnt love christmas time? And to go with that, you have a perfect bgm. Christopher Drake did a fantastic job in combining and serving the dark theme with sleigh bells depicting the atmosphere impeccably. The dialogues are perfect. Voice over....perfect! But wait....there is no Kevin Conroy or Mark Hamill?! Yes, the devs chose to pick Roger Craig Smith (beloved Ezio's voice) and Troy Baker (another genius of the industry) to play young Batman and Joker. Amazingly delivered performance! Both did full justice to their respective characters. I never missed Kevin or Mark during whole game. Roger and Troy are both genius of this industry and glad i could hear their voices as Batman and Joker. Combat stays pretty much the same if you've played previous arkham games. Every gadget is same except for few new ones. What this game really excels is in the You will see one of the best boss fights in this game....as said by many gamers. You can't just buttonmash! Each boss is unique in its own way, each plays differently. Defeating these bosses is very satisfying experience as they can get difficult at times. Only major downside, the side quests/collectibles. I loved finding the nicely hidden Riddler's trophies in Arkham City. It was very satisfying finding each one, as you have to to get that trophy. In Origins, you just throw batarang, and collect data packs or something. Very uninteresting. Anarky spreads some symbols thoughout Origins map for you do discover and some other not so interesting quests/collectibles. Arkham Ciy nails it in this aspect. I didn't encounter any kind of crash or bug or glitch in the game. And it ran pretty smooth on my potato as well. Great job WB! All in all, i love this game. One of the best experience in gaming for me. No wonder Arkham series is considered one of the finest franchise. This game is no less than Arkham City. Both are equally great experience. As i have said for the franchise, I will say it once again: Tip: If you plan on playing Arkham series, either play in the order these games were released or in the order of their own timeline: Origins->Asylum->City.

title: Batman™: Arkham Origins
text: Depending on if this is your first Batman game, this game has two separate reviews. Like with all the other Batman games, the storyline is well written. The villians add a lot of substance and most the time do not come off as simple cameo time. The voice acting is exceptional and diverse. When dealing with the street thugs however, their dialog repeats way to often. You will constantly hear about the guys making fake ID's to do a bank job... Don't worry because he is a professional "and he never make mistakes!" Graphics are top notch just like every other Batman game. And this is where the differences in rating start to change. If you are new to the series, the graphics are easily outstanding. As you go through the game, your suit, to include your cape develops damage showing just how much the Batman does in a night. If you are a verteran, this is the same as all the other games and the only difference is that the detail is a little more polished. Overall, the graphics have not taken much of an increase. In fact, the small extras floating around the city (like papers and trash) are less. The spark effects have been increased through. One thing I can say however is that this game has a lot more graphical glitches in it than the others. Next is the storyline. If this is your first Batman, the story is pretty stable. The ending will leave you fealing left out as though they did not finish the game and just ended it. Which was actually the point as this is the prequal to the first game. So those who have played the other two will enjoy how everything ended up and know exactly what is going to happen next. As far as the controls are concerned, If you are again new to Batman, the controls are very fluid and easy to use. Some of the moves are not completely explained and hope you have experience with the other games to know their full capability on how and when to use them. If you are a veteran, the controls at times seam a bit sluggish at times. One thing I hated about the second game was the Riddler puzzles. The first game made the chalenges insightfull and semi reasonable. The second game just tried to make them as difficult and annoying as possible. The Riddler had his  own optional storyline but was truly annoying to complete. The third game however toned chalenges down and added a bit to the optional storyline. Overall, the game is excellent for new and old players and should be picked up. Considering this is an origins story, you can play this one either first or third.

title: Battle for Blood - Epic battles within 30 seconds!
text: More Reviews @ Battle for Blood came to my attention when I was fixing up a computer for a friend and I was setting it up to have something that their grand-kid could play as opposed to playing flash games and downloading viruses from various websites. Thus Steam was downloaded and some FTP games were installed. I’m a fairly decent fan of Match-3 games in as much as they are more blatantly time-wasters more so than your usual games are. A lot of games will try to give you a deep story where in Match-3 games, the stories are pretty bland and used more as filler between and explaining why the levels exist in the order they do. Battle for Blood is basically the same thing with a mild twist. With so many Match-3’s out there, if you are to make a new one and want it to compete, you’ll have to do something different. What Battle for Blood does is reward you in real-time with units for the fight you are currently engaging in above the Match-3 board. The bigger the match, the larger the number of units are brought into the field. You’ll probably encounter some super BS baddies, but give it time and you’ll end up with some of your own. The flip-side of the coin is that there are “penalties” to using said powerful units… well for you. The computer just does whatever it wants. As you progress you gain access to more powerful units, however there is one more thing you need to pay attention to. Each unit has a cost (which also corresponds to the rate at which their pieces will appear on the board). More powerful units cost a lot less, but you’ll still have to send a level specific amount of units onto the field. Weaker units will fill this need quicker since they have a higher cost. The more powerful units won’t fill this bar much at all. That means to get up to the level specific amount of units, you’ll have to bring more troops. That also means there are more tiles on the board and it will be harder to create large matches or matches at all really. You’ll have to decide if the cost is worth the benefit, and sometimes it is. I didn’t like taking more than 4-5 units in if I didn’t have to. With each round won or lost, you’ll gain money. You’ll be using this to upgrade many aspects of each troop individually.  This is where the grind can come in. Some levels will be designed as difficulty barriers. You’ll probably have to try some of these levels a few times. Some have complained about the grinding in this game, however they have obviously never played a game with real grinding ala Monster Hunter. That said, sometimes upgrading your troops doesn’t guarantee victory. I’ve simply played a level a time or three and suddenly the RNG was with me and I straight wrecked the level that previously trounced me. Whatever works I guess, right? Score Gewd./Tasty! While Battle for Blood does slap you with RNG, it at least isn’t taking math lessons from X-Com. There is some grinding to be found, but it’s really nothing to be worried about since the core concept of the game is rather fun. If you’re having a rough go about the game, mix up your picks. I tended to stick with the low-cost units, healer and one big DPS/tank. Remember that a smaller, but stronger army is better. The only other thing that can get frustrating is earning three starts because it tends to rely on the amount of things you kill. If you don’t get three stars, stay until you do. It’ll be harder if you have to come back with stronger units. If you do well, you can probably destroy all the content in about ten hours. That’s more than some time I’ve spent in games that cost me money.  If you enjoy Match-3 games, you have no real excuse for not playing Battle for Blood. I am waiting for the additional content that Battle for Blood says is coming.
